We need number of CH3 groups in the molecule. But we don't have the molecule given. Possibly the sample is the one at hand, maybe the system has a current compound context. We need to determine CH3 count. Could use NMR spectra to infer? But easier: maybe the molecule is known from previous tasks? Not provided. Could request proton NMR to see methyl signals. Use proton_nmr_spectra tool. That will give peaks; methyl groups appear as singlet around 0.9-1.2 ppm (if aliphatic) or maybe other. But counting peaks may be ambiguous. Could also use carbon NMR to see number of methyl carbons (around 10-30 ppm). Use carbon_nmr_spectra. That may be cheaper? Both are similar cost. Use carbon NMR to count distinct methyl carbon signals. But if symmetry duplicates, number of methyl groups may be less than signals. Hard.

Maybe the molecule is simple known? Could be something like "acetophenone"? Not sure.

We need to get the molecule's structure. Could request HSQC to map. But maybe the simplest is to request proton NMR and count methyl peaks. Let's try proton_nmr_spectra.
